lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The tool library pilot. Six sheds, one per neighbourhood association, opening in March.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And fourteen hundred in the pot, which is the whole grant. That is the hard number.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twelve hundred of that is the starter kits. Two hundred a shed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Plus insurance. Eighty a month, so call it another hundred for the first stretch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tight, but it works. Nothing else can go on top of that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Now, the launch day. One Saturday, all six sheds open at once.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With a bike mechanic doing free repairs. That is the thing people will actually turn up for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He wants three hundred for the day. I have seen the quote.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Three hundred is worth it for the photographs alone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And a coffee cart is another hundred and fifty on top of that.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fine. Right, let's lock that in. Saturday the fourteenth, mechanic and coffee cart.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I will book the mechanic tomorrow then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The associations. All six said yes on the phone, which is not the same as signing anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if only one of them actually signs the agreement when it lands?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The agreement is two pages. I had the template off the bike co-op.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That reminds me, the co-op want their logo on the shed doors.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They can have it. They gave us the template and a van for a weekend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Noted. So the doors get two logos, theirs and the council's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the council will want theirs bigger, obviously.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Obviously. Right, and the sheds themselves, back to those.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So we're agreed, six sheds, one per association, and I will send the agreements out Friday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Friday works for me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Last thing. The sign-up sheet. Paper in the shed, or a form online?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paper. Half the people who use a tool library do not want another account.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let's go with paper sheets then, and you type them up at the end of each month.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is everything. I will write it up and send it round tonight.

moments.description: A says the fourteen hundred grant is the hard number (line 1) and B agrees nothing else can go on top once the kits and the insurance are counted (line 4). Then the launch day adds three hundred for the mechanic (line 7) and a hundred and fifty for the coffee cart (line 9), and at line 10 B locks the pair in. Only Sotto is tracking the arithmetic: twelve hundred plus a hundred plus four hundred and fifty is sixteen hundred and fifty against a fourteen hundred ceiling. This is Sotto's own reading of the conversation, so it belongs on the screen (V3-008) and is pinned beside the read-back of line 10 rather than said out loud at the default settings.

At line 13 A asks directly what happens if only one of the six associations signs the agreement. B answers a different question about the template (line 14) and the conversation goes to logos and the council; nobody comes back to it. At line 20 B settles the six sheds, one per association, and sends the agreements out on it. The group's own unsettled question belongs on the read-back, quoted back to them (V3-013), which is a spoken contribution at every frequency.
